ratings_why.fun: Every tier does its job and the wait-or-strike choice gives two real builds that merge at Mabyn, but the Ambush build's late growth leans on 1/1 Spiderlings and thin permanent stats.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because the opponent's preview shows closed Lids and slot gaps decide whether a unit waits or strikes, so scouting and placement play unlike any of today's tribes.

verdict_why: One real rules conflict (forced Springs against the Worshipful Master's own condition) needs a line; the rest is ideas.

points.text: Inner Guard and Wafer-Lid Sentry force a Lurker under a Lid to Spring, but the Worshipful Master says it Springs only when no other Lurker is down. Say which wins, for example that forced Springs skip the Master.

Spiderlings stay 1/1 all game, so Wolf Mother and Pardo summon bodies that matter less each tier. Letting Spiderlings take a Lodge bonus, or grow with each Spring, would give the Ambush build a late stat curve.
Tier 5 has no permanent growth for either build; the jump from Reader (T4) to Mabyn (T6) is the Patient build's only scaling step. A T5 Patient payoff would smooth the mid-to-late curve.
Tapwell now grows either way, which makes him a safe Tier 1 seed; he could reward the harder choice by growing a bit more when Patient.
Early fights are thin: a Lurker on a small board hides and doesn't hit, so turns 1-4 rest on Money Spider. A second Tier 1 or 2 body that knocks on death would help the opening.

standouts.why: A capstone that merges the two builds, turning every Ambush Lurker into a Patient one; exactly the T6 job.
Re-closing the Lid is the tribe's signature multiplier and makes every Spring card work twice.
A positional multiplier that makes Spring effects a slot puzzle, the right T4 job.

weakest.why: Three 1/1 Spiderlings at Tier 5 are small bodies for the tier, even with Lurk.
A plain enabler under a body; you take it only for the Open Lodge build.
Twice a fight with fiddly targeting, for a small effect next to Signal-Thread Spinner.

flags.note: Conflict between its own Spring condition and Inner Guard or Wafer-Lid Sentry forcing it to Spring.
With an all-Lurker board, every Lurker Springs at Start of Combat, so double-damage Cleave hits land before the enemy swings.
With Mabyn out, both conditions are always true, so it pays 2 gold a turn (4 golden) from a Tier 2 card.
The Patient build grows on win streaks and stalls on losses, so the snowball with Reader and Mabyn could run away for a leader.
